analysis:
The PR is docs-only, with no code changes. docs/developer/test.md (head lines 4438-4656) is unchanged context. docs/provider/attestation.md changes security-relevant policy descriptions.

1) Head ~line 85: the recurring risk-receipt requirement is relaxed for basic serving. A missing or unverified receipt no longer clears an accepted grant, and extra assertions are no longer required. The doc defers to an external darkbloom-platform doc pinned to a commit. Rewards and MDM-removal readiness keep stricter receipt and decision-freshness checks. This conflicts with TB-011, which requires a verified fresh risk receipt for every serving grant. Threat IDs: TB-011, T-053, T-055, A-016.
2) Head ~107-115: a same-process endpoint-resumption challenge is introduced, with no fresh Apple call and platform-side recheck. A native qualification report is cited, but its content was not supplied. The doc states resumption is not enabled in production. This is new attack surface for TB-011 and T-053 (replay and stale grants).
3) Retry and backoff schedules (1m/5m/10m) were removed from the in-repo doc and replaced with external pinned links. The doc says it does not establish what a deployed coordinator runs. The backoff change does not alter authorization (retries grant no permission), so it was not raised as a finding.
4) The logout text honestly states that local deletion does not prove remote token revocation (A-008), a documentation improvement.

The next pass should check the coordinator code and platform repo for how the receipt relaxation and resumption are bounded and fenced. Those sources were not supplied.

findings.detail: The head text says a missing or unverified recurring risk receipt, or a missing risk metric, 'does not clear an accepted, otherwise valid basic serving grant'. It also says no extra assertions are required. It defers to a pinned external platform doc and adds that not every deployment uses the policy. The canonical TB-011 and the base docs require a verified fresh risk receipt for every serving grant, and receipt expiry and renewal deadlines shorten the grant. If the platform coordinator follows the new text, grants could outlive receipt verification. That weakens the credential-continuity and revocation signal (T-053, T-055). Operators and reviewers also cannot tell which policy is live. Fix: update TB-011, A-016 and T-053/T-055 to define the basic-serving versus rewards/MDM-removal receipt split and its bounds. Alternatively, keep the docs aligned with the current requirement until that policy ships.
findings.title: Docs describe a recurring risk-receipt policy that conflicts with the canonical serving requirement

findings.detail: The added text describes a same-process reconnect in which the provider answers an encrypted endpoint-resumption challenge without another Apple call. The platform then rechecks retained evidence and policy. This creates a serving-authorization path that skips fresh assertion verification, which TB-011 treats as required (assertion, nonce and counter, current endpoint and connection binding). The docs themselves note the path is not enabled in production and rely on a report whose content was not supplied. Risks include replaying or rebinding an old grant to a new connection, and extending a grant past the 15-minute freshness window, past receipt expiry, or past revocation after a credential or build change (T-053, T-054). Fix: add the resumption protocol to TB-011/T-053, with explicit bounds on the maximum total lifetime without Apple proof, fencing by revocation and policy generation, endpoint-key binding, and the final-handoff check. Keep it disabled until then.
findings.title: New endpoint-resumption path serves without a fresh Apple call; not covered by the threat model
